name: i18n-ai-translate-sync
description: Keeps every locale file in sync and translates new or changed i18n strings with an AI model (GitHub Copilot or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), using your product glossary for accurate, review-ready translations.

commands.title: Sync Last Commit (the latest commit of the source folder to the ticked destinations)
Sync Locales (sync the source to the ticked destinations)
Set API Key for a Custom AI Endpoint
Improve with My AI Chat (copy prompt)
Show Translation Status (not translated, problems, retry)

i18nSync.enabled.description: Sync automatically after each commit in the source folder's repo, into the ticked destinations (no prompt). Off: nothing happens on commit; use "Sync Last Commit" or the Sync Locales button when you want.

i18nSync.source.description: The folder with the base-language files that strings are synced from, e.g. C:/AppRepo/locales/en (a fallback copy in an application repo) or C:/TranslationRepo/locales/en. Use ~/ for your home folder on macOS/Linux.

i18nSync.destinations.description: Where the source is synced to. Each destination has a folder, a type and a tick. "translate": a folder with one sub-folder per language (i18nSync.locales) that receives translations; "copy": a folder that receives the base language as it is (for example a fallback copy in another repo). Only ticked (enabled) destinations are used; with more than one, Sync Locales asks which to use for each batch (i18nSync.askDestinations).

enumDescriptions: Translate into every language (a folder with one sub-folder per language)
Copy the base language as it is

enabled.description: Tick: include this destination when syncing.

i18nSync.askDestinations.description: When more than one destination is ticked, ask which of them to use each time Sync Locales runs (so one batch can go to one repo and another batch to both).

i18nSync.locales.description: Languages (the sub-folders of every "translate" destination) that receive translations, e.g. ["en","fr","es"]. Include the base language if you want it kept in the destination too.

i18nSync.sourceLocale.description: The base language: the language strings are written in. It is copied as is, never translated, and is the language everything else is translated from.

i18nSync.onlyOwnCommits.description: Ignore commits authored by someone else (e.g. single-commit fast-forward pulls).

i18nSync.backendUrl.description: Hugging Face Space used as the last machine-translation fallback (POST /translate {text, lang}).

i18nSync.backendTimeoutSeconds.description: Backend timeout before falling back to Google (free Spaces can take a while to wake up).

i18nSync.provider.description: Machine-translation fallback, used only when no AI answers. auto = Google first (then the Hugging Face Space if Google is blocked); google = Google only; backend = the Space only.

i18nSync.maxWaitMinutes.description: How long one sync keeps waiting for a translation service (cold-starting backend, rate-limited Google) before writing English for the remaining strings and queuing them for automatic retry. About 2 seconds per string are added on top (at most 30 minutes in all), so large syncs get the time they need.

i18nSync.googleUrl.description: Advanced: use this Google-compatible translate endpoint instead of the two built-in ones (for example a corporate proxy). Leave empty for the default.

i18nSync.contextFile.description: Path of the context file (product description, tone, approved glossary, names to keep). Empty: use i18n-context.json inside the locales folder if it exists. Use "Create Context File from Template" to make one.

i18nSync.ai.enabled.description: Master switch for AI translation. Off: only machine translation (Google, then the Hugging Face Space) is used. Normally left on.

enumDescriptions: Nothing of your own: GitHub Copilot, then the free services
Google Gemini with your free API key
Groq with your free API key
A model running on this computer under Ollama
Any OpenAI-compatible server (base URL, model and key)
i18nSync.ai.provider.description: The AI provider to use after GitHub Copilot. The order is fixed: Copilot, then this provider, then the free fallbacks. The API key is typed on the settings page and kept in VS Code's secret storage.

i18nSync.ai.useCopilot.description: Use GitHub Copilot first when it is available (VS Code only). Turn off to skip Copilot and use your own provider.

i18nSync.ai.allowFreeFallbacks.description: When nothing else can translate, allow the free online fallbacks: a free anonymous AI service (OVHcloud AI Endpoints, EU) and Google Translate. Strings are sent to those services. Off: nothing leaves your machine except to the providers you chose.

i18nSync.ai.copilotModel.description: Which Copilot model to use: "included" (models normally not charged as premium requests on paid plans, e.g. GPT-4.1), "best" (prefers Claude / GPT-5; may use premium requests), or part of a model name such as "claude-sonnet".

i18nSync.ai.reviewPass.description: Send each batch to the model a second time to proofread the draft (more accurate, one extra request per batch).

i18nSync.ai.endpoint.description: Base URL of the "custom" provider (an OpenAI-compatible server, e.g. https://api.groq.com/openai/v1), or the address of Ollama when it is not http://127.0.0.1:11434.

i18nSync.ai.model.description: Model name(s). Custom: required. Gemini and Groq: optional override of the built-in list. Ollama: optional, otherwise the best installed model is used. Several models can be listed, separated by commas; they share the key and the next one is used when one is limited.

i18nSync.memory.enabled.description: Reuse translations that already exist in the destination repo when exactly the same base-language text appears again (free and consistent). Unconfirmed machine translations are never reused.

scripts.compile: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js
scripts.package: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js --production
scripts.test: npm run check-types:test && npm run test:unit
